newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Selecta aims to extend 12 pct EBIT growth.
newsitem.headline: Selecta aims to extend 12 pct EBIT growth.

text.p: Selecta, the vending machine division that Valora Holding AG is spinning off via a share issue, said it wanted to keep earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) growing at its 12 percent average in 1997.
Net profit will grow more slowly than EBIT in 1997, Selecta chief Thies Schneider told reporters.
"EBIT has grown by an average of around 12 percent in the past. Our goal is to be able to maintain this trend," he said.
Net profit would not grow as quickly, he added, noting its tax burden in France would grow after years of being offset against earlier losses.
He did not give any specific forecast for net profit growth.
Selecta aims for a dividend pay-out ratio around 20 percent, he said. Valora is paying the costs of the public offering. Selecta would not have to pick up any restructuring costs.
Selecta's EBIT rose 17 percent in 1996 to 40.7 million Swiss francs. Net profit was 29.4 million. -- Zurich +41 1 631 7340
